name: Memory chips (HBM)
one_line: Stacks of DRAM bonded into a tower, sold so an AI chip can be fed data fast enough to keep its compute busy.
sells: High-bandwidth memory: layers of DRAM stacked on a logic base die and sold to AI chip makers
customers: AI chip and GPU designers (NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Google), who mount HBM right next to the processor
suppliers: DRAM wafer fabs, advanced-packaging and through-silicon-via tooling, and foundries for the HBM4 logic base die

revenue.note: Forecasts, not an audited actual. BofA sees $54.6B in 2026 (+58% YoY), cited on SK Hynix's newsroom; Yole estimates ~$60B (+~70%) up from ~$35B in 2025. Supply is sold out, so revenue tracks capacity and price more than demand.

structure.why: Only three firms in the world ship HBM in volume. SK Hynix has led on HBM3E; Micron has pulled ahead of Samsung, and Samsung's HBM4 is now closing the gap.
structure.hhi_note: Sum of squared Q2 2026 shares (62, 21, 17) from Counterpoint Research as reported by Future of Korea / Astute Group. Basis is reported variously as revenue and as bit shipments, so treat the HHI as approximate; a fourth entrant (CXMT) has no measurable share yet.

econ: Barriers to entry. Making HBM needs both leading-edge DRAM and advanced 3D stacking (through-silicon vias), which only three companies can do at scale, so the market is a global oligopoly. Because demand outruns capacity, output is sold out a year ahead and the makers, not the buyers, hold the pricing power.

companies.name: SK Hynix
companies.share_basis: overall HBM share, Q2 2026 (Counterpoint Research, reported by Future of Korea / Astute Group); basis reported variously as revenue and bit shipments
companies.note: The HBM3E leader and NVIDIA's main supplier. Counterpoint says its growth slowed in Q3 2026 as Samsung's HBM4 gained.

companies.name: Micron
companies.share_basis: overall HBM share, Q2 2026 (Counterpoint Research, reported by Future of Korea / Astute Group); basis reported variously as revenue and bit shipments
companies.note: Overtook Samsung for second place in Q2 2026 per Counterpoint; ramping HBM3E and HBM4 for NVIDIA and other AI-chip clients.

companies.name: Samsung
companies.share_basis: overall HBM share, Q2 2026 (Counterpoint Research, reported by Future of Korea / Astute Group); basis reported variously as revenue and bit shipments
companies.note: Lagged on HBM3E but its HBM4 is well received; Counterpoint expects Samsung to challenge for the HBM lead in 2027.

companies.name: CXMT
companies.note: China's largest DRAM maker and an aspiring HBM entrant; no material HBM share in 2026 sources checked.

products_note: Flagship products as of Nov 2026. AI-lab and chip products checked against 2026 launch coverage; products for banks, card networks, utilities and others are long-standing lines from general knowledge, not individually cited.
